title: Body Has The Real Details
description: A notification that just says "something happened" is useless — a customer reading their payment-failed alert should be able to tell which shipment or invoice it's actually about.
successCondition: Pay an invoice with the decline test card. After waiting past the queue delay, querying the notifications table via `npm run db:psql` for the resulting payment.failed row confirms the body column contains specific, non-generic content tying it to the actual event — e.g. a dollar amount, currency, or failure reason string, not just a static "Your payment failed" with no identifying detail. Cross-check the body's amount/currency against the actual invoice.amountCents/currency you paid.
hints: Check what fields the notify() call site for payment failure (apps/api/src/modules/billing/service.ts or wherever pay() lives) actually interpolates into the body string — the exact wording matters less than whether it's genuinely event-specific.
The decline test card number is documented in docs/api/billing.md.
